content: During pregnancy, an obstetric ultrasound scan can be utilized to screen for congenital heart disease (CHD) in the fetus. This screening is typically conducted around the 20th week of gestation, as the fetal heart structures at this stage are sufficiently developed and large enough to allow for clearer imaging. If there is a suspicion of CHD based on the initial ultrasound findings, the pregnant individual is referred for a fetal echocardiography. This is a more detailed and diagnostic ultrasound examination performed by a specialist cardiologist. Advances in medical technology and expertise now enable specialists to screen for CHD as early as the 14th week of pregnancy, particularly if there are additional risk factors, such as a family history of CHD.
